text: Koloman Bedeković (Hungarian: Kálmán Bedekovich; 13 October 1818 – 10 August 1889) was a Croatian politician who served as Minister without portfolio of Croatian Affairs twice, from 1868 to 1871 and from 1876 to 1889. He played a key role in the creation of the Croatian-Hungarian Agreement. In 1871, he was appointed Ban of Croatia-Slavonia. Bedeković led the Croatian Unionist Party and opposed Croatia's independence. As ban, he called parliamentary elections in 1871. The People's Party won the election, prompting Bedeković to prorogue the Parliament of Croatia three times to block its authority. This obstruction led to the Rakovica Revolt. Due to his failure to convene the previous parliament, Bedeković was removed from the position of ban and replaced by Ivan Mažuranić, the first non-noble ban.
